idiom_name: tagged sentinel item in a hand-rolled ring buffer under pthread mutex + condition variable
implementation_notes: C has neither a queue nor a close primitive: build the queue (typically a bounded ring buffer) guarded by a pthread_mutex_t and a pthread_cond_t, and make the poison pill an item tagged after the last work item. Consumers block in pthread_cond_wait inside a predicate loop (the queue is non-empty) and exit when they dequeue the stop tag; because pthread_cond_wait may wake spuriously and several consumers may share the same condition variable, the predicate must be re-checked every iteration and one pill must be enqueued for each blocked consumer (or a shared stop flag broadcast with pthread_cond_broadcast). The tag field - not a magic pointer value - is what keeps the sentinel collision-free with real payloads.
pitfalls: pthread_cond_wait can wake spuriously: always wait in a while (predicate) loop, never behind a single if.
One pill wakes one consumer; with several consumers enqueue one per consumer (or broadcast) - otherwise the remaining threads stay blocked.
The stop tag must be an explicit field or enum; a NULL payload works only if no legitimate item can ever be NULL.
The condition functions are not async-signal-safe, so a signal handler must not enqueue pills directly - hand the request to a normal thread first.
